FuzzyClass

A comprehensive family of probability-based fuzzy and non-fuzzy classifiers.

Classification problems involve assigning categorical labels to data instances based on observed features. In real-world applications, classes often overlap, boundaries are imprecise, and measurements carry uncertainty. Traditional Bayesian classifiers assume rigid distributional parameters and crisp class assignments.

FuzzyClass addresses these challenges by unifying Fuzzy Set Theory (μ∈[0,1]\mu \in [0, 1]) with Probabilistic Naive Bayes classification. By leveraging soft membership degrees, fuzzy parameters (triangular and trapezoidal), and geometric distance weighting, FuzzyClass delivers robust, interpretable, and high-performance classification for complex and ambiguous data.

A complete manual showcasing all classifiers and mathematical details is available at the CRAN FuzzyClass Reference Manual.

What’s New in Version 0.3.0

  • 🧱 R6 classes: every classifier is now an R6 class (e.g. FuzzyGaussianNaiveBayesModel) with $new(), $fit(), $predict() and $set_params(). The functional interface (FuzzyGaussianNaiveBayes(train, cl) + predict()) still works and gives the same predictions.
  • 💬 Friendly training messages: $fit() tells you which model is being trained, on how much data, and how long it took. Silence it with verbose = FALSE or options(FuzzyClass.verbose = FALSE).
  • 🔗 tidymodels support: the new parsnip model fuzzy_naive_bayes() exposes all classifiers as engines, ready for workflows, recipes, rsample, tune and yardstick, including tuning of fuzzy, alpha_cut and ranking_method.

What’s New in Version 0.2.0

  • 🐞 Correct class labelling: parameters and predicted labels now always follow the same class order (factor levels). Previous development code could mislabel predictions when the training data were not sorted by class.
  • 📐 Estimation aligned with the literature: exact Gamma maximum likelihood, unbounded Beta shapes, Geometric pmf consistent with its estimator, Binomial n >= max(x), class-wise sample sizes in the fuzzy-parameter confidence intervals and nested alpha-cuts in PoiNBFuzzyParam.
  • ⚡ Vectorized predictions: prediction and fuzzy-number ranking (metd = 1:5) are vectorized over all observations, about 100× faster than version 0.1.7.
  • 🪶 Lighter dependencies: dplyr, purrr, tibble, tidyr, rlang, parallel, foreach and doParallel are no longer required (cores is kept only for backward compatibility).

Available Classifiers (Taxonomy)

FuzzyClass provides 17 classifiers and a fuzzy rule-based system, categorized by feature type and modeling paradigm. Each classifier X has the functional interface X(train, cl), the R6 class XModel and an engine of fuzzy_naive_bayes():

Classifier Paradigm Description tidymodels engine
FuzzyGaussianNaiveBayes Continuous Gaussian Naive Bayes weighted by fuzzy membership degrees. "gaussian"
GauNBFuzzyParam Continuous Gaussian Naive Bayes with fuzzy parameters (μ̃,σ̃2\tilde{\mu}, \tilde{\sigma}^2) across 5 estimation methods. "gaussian_fuzzy_param"
FuzzyExponentialNaiveBayes Continuous Exponential Naive Bayes with fuzzy memberships for positive continuous features. "exponential"
ExpNBFuzzyParam Continuous Exponential Naive Bayes with fuzzy rate parameters. "exponential_fuzzy_param"
FuzzyGammaNaiveBayes Continuous Gamma Naive Bayes with fuzzy memberships for skewed continuous data. "gamma"
DWFuzzyGammaNaiveBayes Continuous Double-Weighted Fuzzy Gamma Naive Bayes. "dw_gamma"
FuzzyBetaNaiveBayes Continuous Beta Naive Bayes for continuous features bounded in (0,1)(0, 1) (rates/proportions). "beta"
FuzzyTriangularNaiveBayes Continuous Naive Bayes with triangular membership functions. "triangular"
FuzzyTrapezoidalNaiveBayes Continuous Naive Bayes with trapezoidal membership functions. "trapezoidal"
FuzzyPoissonNaiveBayes Discrete / Count Poisson Naive Bayes with fuzzy memberships for integer count data. "poisson"
PoiNBFuzzyParam Discrete / Count Poisson Naive Bayes with fuzzy rate parameters λ̃\tilde{\lambda}. "poisson_fuzzy_param"
FuzzyBinomialNaiveBayes Discrete / Count Binomial Naive Bayes with fuzzy memberships for binary/trial counts. "binomial"
FuzzyHipergeometricNaiveBayes Discrete / Count Hypergeometric Naive Bayes for sampling without replacement from finite populations. "hypergeometric"
DWFuzzyHipergeometricNaiveBayes Discrete / Count Double-Weighted Hypergeometric Naive Bayes. "dw_hypergeometric"
FuzzyGeoNaiveBayes Geometric Naive Bayes with distance-based geometric fuzzy memberships. "geometric"
FuzzyNaiveBayes General Generalized fuzzy Naive Bayes supporting continuous and categorical features. "naive"
FuzzyBayesRule Decision Rule Fuzzy Bayes decision rule classifier. "bayes_rule"
FuzzyRuleBasedSystem Inference Rule Fuzzy rule-based inference and classification system. —

Installation

Stable Version from CRAN

You can install the released version of FuzzyClass from CRAN:

install.packages("FuzzyClass")

Development Version from GitHub

To install the latest development version:

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("leapigufpb/FuzzyClass")

Dependencies

FuzzyClass is designed with minimal, stable, and battle-tested dependencies automatically installed by R:

  • caTools
  • cli
  • e1071
  • EnvStats
  • MASS
  • maxLik
  • mvtnorm
  • R6
  • Rdpack
  • rootSolve

The tidymodels packages (parsnip, dials, tune, …) are optional: install them to use fuzzy_naive_bayes().

Quick Start & Examples

1. Data Preparation

We demonstrate package functionality using the built-in VirtualRealityData dataset:

library(FuzzyClass)

# Load dataset
data(VirtualRealityData)
df <- as.data.frame(VirtualRealityData)

# Split into Training (70%) and Testing (30%) sets
set.seed(123)
split <- caTools::sample.split(df[, 4], SplitRatio = 0.7)
Train <- subset(df, split == TRUE)
Test  <- subset(df, split == FALSE)

X_train <- Train[, -4]
y_train <- Train[, 4]
X_test  <- Test[, -4]
y_test  <- Test[, 4]

2. Gaussian Naive Bayes with Fuzzy Parameters (GauNBFuzzyParam)

Fit a Gaussian model where mean and variance are represented as fuzzy numbers:

# Fit model using fuzzy estimation method 2
fit_fgnb <- GauNBFuzzyParam(train = X_train, cl = y_train, metd = 2, cores = 1)
#> ℹ Gaussian Naive Bayes with Fuzzy Parameters: 420 observations, 3 predictors and 3 classes
#> ℹ Training the model: estimating its parameters
#> ✔ Model trained successfully [31ms]
#> 

# Predict classes
pred_classes <- predict(fit_fgnb, X_test)

# Confusion Matrix
conf_mat <- table(Actual = y_test, Predicted = pred_classes)
conf_mat
#>       Predicted
#> Actual  1  2  3
#>      1 55  4  1
#>      2  8 34 18
#>      3  1  9 50

# Classification Accuracy
accuracy <- sum(diag(conf_mat)) / sum(conf_mat)
cat(sprintf("Test Accuracy: %.2f%%\n", accuracy * 100))
#> Test Accuracy: 77.22%

You can also extract the full posterior membership / probability matrix:

# Extract prediction probability matrix
prob_matrix <- predict(fit_fgnb, X_test, type = "matrix")
head(prob_matrix)
#>              1           2            3
#> [1,] 0.4991627 0.376053403 1.247839e-01
#> [2,] 0.9942344 0.005757106 8.478896e-06
#> [3,] 0.9818783 0.009466896 8.654851e-03
#> [4,] 0.9943634 0.005634324 2.298521e-06
#> [5,] 0.5559862 0.433612780 1.040104e-02
#> [6,] 0.9520142 0.013665813 3.432000e-02

3. Continuous Fuzzy Gaussian Naive Bayes (FuzzyGaussianNaiveBayes)

Fit a Gaussian Naive Bayes classifier where observations have fuzzy membership degrees:

# Fit standard fuzzy Gaussian Naive Bayes
fit_gnb <- FuzzyGaussianNaiveBayes(train = X_train, cl = y_train)
#> ℹ Fuzzy Gaussian Naive Bayes (Zadeh-based): 420 observations, 3 predictors and 3 classes
#> ℹ Training the model: estimating its parameters
#> ✔ Model trained successfully [16ms]
#> 

# Predict classes on test set
pred_gnb <- predict(fit_gnb, X_test)

# Confusion matrix
table(Actual = y_test, Predicted = pred_gnb)
#>       Predicted
#> Actual  1  2  3
#>      1 58  2  0
#>      2  7 50  3
#>      3  0 10 50

4. The R6 Interface

Every classifier is an R6 class. Create the model, train it (a message tells you what is happening) and predict:

model <- FuzzyGammaNaiveBayesModel$new(fuzzy = TRUE)
model$fit(train = X_train, cl = y_train)
#> ℹ Fuzzy Gamma Naive Bayes: 420 observations, 3 predictors and 3 classes
#> ℹ Training the model: estimating its parameters
#> ✔ Model trained successfully [6ms]
#> 
model
#> <FuzzyGammaNaiveBayes> Fuzzy Gamma Naive Bayes
#> ✔ Trained on 420 observations in 0.002s
#>   Hyperparameters: fuzzy = TRUE
#>   Predictors (3): V1, V2, V3
#>   Classes (3): 1, 2, 3

head(model$predict(X_test))
#> [1] 1 1 1 1 1 1
#> Levels: 1 2 3
head(model$predict(X_test, type = "prob"))
#>              1            2            3
#> [1,] 0.9084371 9.153798e-02 2.487652e-05
#> [2,] 0.9998998 1.002413e-04 6.140526e-11
#> [3,] 0.9942020 5.797331e-03 7.118546e-07
#> [4,] 0.9999186 8.141746e-05 4.390692e-11
#> [5,] 0.8022878 1.976974e-01 1.476847e-05
#> [6,] 0.9729373 2.706046e-02 2.218717e-06

Hyperparameters can be changed with $set_params(), and the calls can be chained:

model$set_params(fuzzy = FALSE)$fit(X_train, y_train, verbose = FALSE)
mean(model$predict(X_test) == y_test)
#> [1] 0.8777778

5. Using FuzzyClass with tidymodels

fuzzy_naive_bayes() is a parsnip model whose engines are the FuzzyClass classifiers, so it plugs into workflows, recipes, resampling and tuning:

library(tidymodels)

vr <- VirtualRealityData |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(V4 = factor(V4))

set.seed(123)
vr_split <- initial_split(vr, prop = 0.7, strata = V4)

spec <- fuzzy_naive_bayes(alpha_cut = tune(), ranking_method = tune()) |>
  set_engine("gaussian_fuzzy_param")

wf <- workflow() |>
  add_formula(V4 ~ .) |>
  add_model(spec)

options(FuzzyClass.verbose = FALSE) # quiet while tuning
tuned <- tune_grid(wf, resamples = vfold_cv(training(vr_split), v = 5, strata = V4), grid = 5)
show_best(tuned, metric = "accuracy", n = 3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 8
#>   alpha_cut ranking_method .metric  .estimator  mean     n std_err .config      
#>       <dbl>          <int> <chr>    <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>        
#> 1    0.0001              2 accuracy multiclass 0.788     5 0.0121  pre0_mod1_po…
#> 2    0.0501              1 accuracy multiclass 0.786     5 0.00842 pre0_mod3_po…
#> 3    0.0750              5 accuracy multiclass 0.786     5 0.00842 pre0_mod4_po…

final <- finalize_workflow(wf, select_best(tuned, metric = "accuracy")) |>
  last_fit(vr_split)
collect_metrics(final)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   .metric     .estimator .estimate .config        
#>   <chr>       <chr>          <dbl> <chr>          
#> 1 accuracy    multiclass     0.783 pre0_mod0_post0
#> 2 roc_auc     hand_till      0.918 pre0_mod0_post0
#> 3 brier_class multiclass     0.156 pre0_mod0_post0

How to Contribute

Contributions, bug reports, and suggestions are very welcome!

  1. Fork the FuzzyClass repository.
  2. Create a feature branch: git checkout -b feature/my-new-feature.
  3. Commit your changes: git commit -am 'Add new feature'.
  4. Push to the branch: git push origin feature/my-new-feature.
  5. Submit a Pull Request.

Reporting Issues

If you encounter any issues or unexpected behavior, please submit an issue on GitHub: 👉 https://github.com/leapigufpb/FuzzyClass/issues

Please provide a reproducible example (reprex) and session information (sessionInfo()).
